title: Sierra Pharma on-prem Terraform playbook + scaling & upgrade assumptions
content:
Executive summary:

This working playbook captures the current recommended Terraform module layout, sizing assumptions, and a staged upgrade plan for the Sierra Pharmaceuticals VPC / on-prem private deployment. Target is to support: 8k concurrent inference QPS equivalent (small request sizes), 99th percentile latency <= 250ms for 7B/13B models, and predictable throughput for batch workloads used by analytics. This doc is a living draft for the SRE & infra teams and will feed the formal customer proposal.

Goals and constraints:
- No public ingress: all traffic to Redwood Private control plane via customer-managed Transit Gateway + IPsec tunnels.
- Data residency: all model artifacts and logs must remain in customer VPC/storage.
- KMS/HSM: customer requires HSM-backed KMS for model keys.
- Air-gapped optionality for on-prem compute nodes; initial deployment will use VPC-connected colo with egress restrictions.
- Rolling upgrades preferred; acceptable brief (~10–15min) degraded throughput windows for model swapovers.

Baseline workload assumptions (input for sizing):
- Primary model fleet: 7B (Llama2-like) and 13B (Llama2-like) for low-latency endpoints. Occasional 70B large-batch jobs for nightly analytics.
- Average request: 60 tokens in + 40 tokens generated (100 tokens total) for interactive endpoints.
- Peak concurrent interactive sessions: 400 active sessions with soft burst to 1k for < 10 minutes.
- Target sustained throughput for batch jobs: 10k tokens/sec over scheduled window.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 250ms for 7B/13B endpoints.

Hardware and instance guidance (recommendation):
- Serving nodes (low-latency): NVIDIA A10G or H100 L4 equivalent where available; prefer 1 GPU per node for better tail latency and graceful drain.
  - 7B model: 1x A10G (24GB) with 64GB host RAM handles ~40 concurrent low-latency sessions.
  - 13B model: 1x A100 40GB or H100 L4 80GB recommended; expect ~12–18 concurrent low-latency sessions.
- Batch/analytics nodes: A100 80GB pool, autoscaled for scheduled nightly jobs.
- Storage: model artifacts on customer S3-compatible storage (minio) with 3x replicas; local SSD scratch on nodes (NVMe) 1–2TB for caching.
- Networking: 25Gbps NIC minimum per node; recommend 100Gbps for GPU racks connecting to model storage.

Sizing snapshot (initial cluster):
- Low-latency pool: 12 nodes x A10G (serve 7B endpoints) + 8 nodes x A100 40GB (serve 13B endpoints).
- Batch pool: 4 x A100 80GB (scale to 12 for nightly jobs).
- Control plane: 3 m5.large Linux VMs (or equivalent on-prem control VMs) running Redwood Private control components, HA proxy, and monitoring agents.
- Redis/KV (state): 3-node cluster on dedicated VMs, 64GB RAM each (or managed equivalent).

Terraform module notes and layout (how we structure infra as code):
- module naming: modules/private/controlplane, modules/private/gpu-nodepool, modules/private/networking, modules/private/storage, modules/private/kms-integration.
- remote state: customer S3-compatible backend + DynamoDB for locks (or consul if customer prefers). Recommend separate state per environment: sierra-dev, sierra-staging, sierra-prod.
- providers: aws (for VPC/TGW if hybrid), kubernetes, local-exec for bespoke hooks; pin provider versions in versions.tf to avoid drift.
- module inputs to standardize: node_gpu_type, node_count_min, node_count_max, instance_profile, storage_endpoint, kms_key_arn, network_cidr, transit_gateway_id.
- example variables snippet (store in variables.tf in module root):
  - variable "node_gpu_type" { type = string default = "a10g" }
  - variable "node_count_min" { type = number default = 2 }
  - variable "storage_endpoint" { type = string }

State & secrets handling:
- Use customer-managed KMS to encrypt Terraform state; do not export keys to Redwood.
- Secrets stored in vault (customer HashiCorp Vault or customer KMS-backed secret store). Modules should accept secret references, not raw secrets.

Upgrade plan (high level, zero-touch & safe rollback):
1) Preflight checks
   - Run terraform plan in staging against a cloned state.
   - Validate module version compatibility (terraform-docs and tflint checks).
   - Smoke test baseline endpoints against staging.
2) Canary nodes
   - Deploy new nodepool module with small capacity (2 nodes) and mark nodes with canary tag.
   - Route 2–5% of traffic (weighted routing) to canary via control plane rollout policy.
   - Run perf tests including tail-latency & KV-cache regression checks.
3) Gradual roll (if canary good)
   - Scale up new nodepool in batches (25% increments). Drain older nodes per batch, allowing eviction of cached KV state.
   - Monitor p99/p95 and SLI alerts; abort and rollback if thresholds exceeded for >5 minutes.
4) Post-upgrade validation
   - Run regression eval suite (prompt set for Sierra Pharma).
   - Validate billing/cost metrics and autoscaling behavior.
5) Rollback plan
   - If canary fails, remove canary nodepool and re-route traffic to original nodes.
   - If full rollout issues detected, revert terraform state to pre-upgrade state object (via remote-state snapshot) and redeploy.

Operational runbook snippets (quick):
- Draining nodes: mark node unschedulable in kube, wait for in-flight requests to finish, then cordon and terminate.
- Model swap: upload model artifact to storage endpoint with versioned path, update model manifest in control plane, then trigger model hot-reload on target nodepool.
- Emerg rollback: shift routing to hosted Redundancy endpoint with customer approval for up to 30 minutes (policy for disaster recovery).

Open questions & outstanding assumptions to confirm with customer:
- KMS/HSM provider: Yubico HSM vs AWS CloudHSM (customer preference drives integration pattern).
- Network egress policy: does customer allow intermittent outbound to Redwood control plane IP addresses or must we use VPC peering/transit only?
- On-prem rack limits: power/thermal constraints could change recommended node counts per rack.
- Acceptance tests: customer to provide 3 canonical prompt sets for evals and SLO thresholds.

Customer Q&A (answers drafted for call):
Q: Can we support 70B models on-prem?
A: Yes, but requires 80GB+ GPU memory (A100 80GB / H100) and will be placed on the batch pool or a dedicated nodegroup. Latency will be higher; recommend using 70B for non-interactive workloads or async jobs.

Q: How are Terraform upgrades handled if module API changes?
A: We version modules semantically, run automated migration scripts in a staging workspace, and require explicit migrations for breaking changes. Documented migration steps live in the terraform-modules repo.

Action items / next steps:
- [Ava] Finalize node counts after getting power/thermal constraints from Sierra infra (due: 2025-11-20).
- [Diego] Produce a terraform workspace example (sierra-prod) with remote state config & sample variables (due: 2025-11-25).
- [Maya] Draft HSM integration diagram and KMS usage pattern (due: 2025-11-28).
- [Ops] Run a canary test in staging with real prompt set and report perf (target: 2026-01-10).

Notes / rationale: many decisions favor one-GPU-per-node for lower latency & simpler CUDA memory management; while packing multiple GPUs per node is more cost-efficient in some datacenter contexts, it increases tail-latency complexity and complicates draining during updates. We recommend starting conservative and iterating after a production run.

Appendix (quick references):
- Terraform module PR with example inputs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/438
- Design ticket: INFRA-7821
- Staging runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Sierra-Pharma-CR

Draft status comments: this document is intentionally pragmatic and contains open assumptions. Please add any constraints from Sierra Pharma infra team to the Confluence thread linked above and note changes in the terraform workspace checklist.
